Hey @ofc587a87, Streamlit version 1.41.1 does not exist. The latest one is 1.40.0, see the pip release history here: https://pypi.org/project/streamlit/#history
Could you please double-check the versions you are using?

I can confirm that this happens on the latest streamlit version 1.41.0 that was released on the 10th of december.
Downgrading to the previous version 1.40.2 resolves the issue for me.
The error happens on firefox, chrome and edge, for any streamlit app.

I'm seeing the same error. I upgraded from 1.40.2 to 1.41.0. Even a simple hello world app fails:

# Error message

`Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript module script but the server responded with a MIME type of "text/plain". Strict MIME type checking is enforced for module scripts per HTML spec.`

# app.py

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("Hello, world!")
```

Thanks for providing the details and the poetry lock. I tried to reproduce the issue on my Windows virtual machine, but was not successful. Are you all on a Windows machine?
I am wondering whether perhaps the Registry's mimetype might be wrong, see [this thread](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/32350#issuecomment-525115571) and this issue/PR we had in the past: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/9390
When executing the command explained [here](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/32350#issuecomment-525115571), do you see any output? 
I am not sure yet what change in the Streamlit version could have triggered this issue to surface 🤔 

Edit: It might be the first prod build we did with `vite` instead of `webpack` after the migration: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/commit/6f0ff6090596d700e1c8cc4d427a2dc3a55a9fc7
I am wondering whether this changed anything. Searching the web reveals a few reports of wrong mime-types in combination with vite, e.g. [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/75204349/vite-serving-shader-file-with-wrong-none-mime-type), but it might be a false flag.

Would someone be open to share screenshots from the Network Tab or so, so that we can have a look at the mimetype?

Hi, Yes I can confirm this is on windows.
Executing
reg query HKCR\.js /v "Content Type"

returns:

    Content Type    REG_SZ    text/plain

Awesome, thanks for confirming! A fix should then be to set the mimetype in the registry correctly, but besides that we will try to find out what let the issue surface now for the new Streamlit version. I suspect that some vite-metadata or so is different to what webpack produced in the past.

I have just compared the `index.html` files for version `1.40.1` and `1.41.0` and the new version has `type="module"` set in the script tag. Perhaps this has changed something.

issue.body:
## Describe your changes

Python/Tornado uses `mimetypes.guess_type` to determine the content type. On some Windows machines, the registry (which Python uses to get the mimetype) is misconfigured leading to issues on the frontend. We have solutions in other request handlers, namely the custom component handler. The solution is to add the mimetypes explicitly on Server load, so that no issue exists on the request handlers.

Python pretty much says there is [nothing they plan to do](https://bugs.python.org/issue32462).

Tornado suggests [adding the mimetype](https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/issues/1690) like we do to confirm.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes #10004

## Testing Plan

- Python unit tests for the request handlers that rely on this explicitly.
